policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath, or not?' is a direct question; an interrogative Ei has no English exponent, so the ASV wording renders either reading identically.
ASV closes the question with 'or not', rendering the base's e ou; RP's bare therapeuein leaves nothing for those words.
ASV reads simply 'And he said unto them'; the ASV renders apokritheis explicitly ('answering spake', v.3), so the added participle is absent here.
ASV 'fallen into a well' renders the simple and the compounded verb alike; the prefix has no separate English exponent. The mapped note concerns son/ass, not this unit.
ASV 'on a sabbath day' is indefinite English that neither requires nor excludes the article, and the preposition is unrendered as such; nothing distinguishes the three readings.
ASV 'they could not answer again unto these things' supplies no indirect object; RP's auto would appear as 'answer him again'.
ASV 'he may say to thee' renders the future indicative and the aorist subjunctive alike after the temporal clause.
ASV 'in the presence of all that sit at meat with thee' renders panton, which RP omits.
The variants differ only in Greek word order; ASV 'lest haply they also bid thee again' fixes English order independently.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'and a recompense be made thee' renders either sequence.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'when thou makest a feast' renders either sequence.
ASV 'Blessed is he that shall eat bread' renders the indefinite and the simple relative alike.
ASV 'shall eat bread' renders arton; ariston would be a meal/dinner, which the ASV does not say.
ASV 'A certain man made a great supper' renders imperfect and aorist alike; English past tense does not distinguish aspect here.
ASV 'for all things are now ready' has an explicit 'all'; the base's bare hetoima estin would yield only 'things are ready'.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'they all with one consent began to make excuse' renders either sequence.
ASV 'I must needs go out and see it' coordinates the two verbs in idiomatic English, which renders the participle-plus-infinitive as readily as the two coordinated infinitives.
ASV 'And the servant came' has no demonstrative; RP's ekeinos would appear as 'that servant'.
ASV lists 'the poor and maimed and blind and lame' - blind before lame, the base order; RP reverses the pair.
ASV 'what thou didst command is done' renders the relative ho as object of the command; RP's hos would give 'as thou didst command'.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'that my house may be filled' renders either sequence.
ASV ends the verse at 'shall taste of my supper'; RP's added clause 'for many are called, but few chosen' is absent from the ASV.
ASV 'hateth not his own father' uses the emphatic reflexive 'his own', rendering heautou; the plain possessive autou would give 'his father'.
ASV 'yea, and his own life also' renders the connective either way; te kai and de kai are not distinguished by this English.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'his own life also' renders either sequence.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'he cannot be my disciple' renders either sequence.
ASV opens the verse 'Whosoever doth not bear' with no connective; RP/Treg's kai would appear as 'And whosoever'.
ASV 'his own cross' marks a reflexive, excluding the plain possessive autou (r01); heautou and its contracted form hauton are indistinguishable in English.
ASV 'which of you, desiring to build a tower' does not show whether the participle carried the article.
ASV 'whether he have wherewith to complete it' gives no exponent for an article before the prepositional phrase.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'begin to mock him' renders either sequence.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'as he goeth to encounter another king in war' renders either sequence.
ASV 'will not sit down first and take counsel' is future, matching bouleusetai; the ASV renders the parallel present in v.28 as 'doth not first sit down and count'.
ASV 'to meet him that cometh against him' renders either compound of the verb; the prefixes are not distinguished in English.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'while the other is yet a great way off' renders either sequence.
ASV 'asketh conditions of peace' supplies 'conditions' as the sense of the phrase whether or not the article stood; the article has no separate exponent.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'he cannot be my disciple' renders either sequence.
ASV 'Salt therefore is good' renders oun, which RP omits.
ASV 'but if even the salt have lost its savor' renders the ascensive kai as 'even'; RP omits it.
